text: Output must include missing_fields, open_questions, recommended_next_steps, and supporting_playbook_citations. Cite chunk_ids used.
Avoid hallucinations: do not invent codes, dates, diagnoses, or contract terms. Missing info becomes open questions + concrete request steps.
Confidence gating: if denial taxonomy confidence is low, prefer an information request plan over definitive language.
CO-16 style: first action is to identify what is missing. Prioritize itemized bill, operative report, clinical notes, and any authorization identifiers.
If denial_text is sparse, request full EOB/ERA detail, payer portal denial detail, and any remark codes tied to the denial.
CO-29 style: validate dates; request proof of original submission and payer acknowledgment. Flag contradictions (e.g., CO-29 with very low days_since_denial).
CO-50 style: focus on clinical rationale. If ICDs missing, list as open question and request clinical evidence (H&P, notes, imaging, conservative therapy history).
Narratives should avoid legal citations for this challenge; stay grounded in the record and missing evidence.
CO-97 style: identify primary vs secondary procedures; request line-level EOB and bundling rationale; do not invent modifiers.
CO-27 style: confirm coverage timeline; request eligibility verification / coverage dates; flag NON_ERISA scope if applicable.
CO-45: compute coverage_ratio = paid_amount/billed_amount. If coverage_ratio >= 0.70 (challenge rule), recommend DO NOT PURSUE.
CO-45 when <0.70: request contract terms/fee schedule, allowables, repricing notes; summarize billed, paid, delta.
For OOD/unknown denial codes, be explicit about uncertainty and prioritize information requests (EOB detail, payer portal notes, attachments).
